reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n with n >= 2 and every a in real n-dimensional Euclidean space with ||a|| = 1, the real-valued function f_a(x) = (1 - ||x||^2) / ||x - a||^n is harmonic on the complement of {a}. Precisely, for every x in real n-dimensional Euclidean space with x != a, f_a is C^2 at x and there exists a neighborhood U of x such that the actual Euclidean Laplacian of f_a is zero at every point of U. The Laplacian is the orthonormal trace of the second Frechet derivative. No conclusion is asserted at a.
objects: A dimension n, a unit vector a, the real-valued function f_a(x) = (1 - ||x||^2) / ||x - a||^n, and the punctured Euclidean space {a}^c.
domains: n is a natural number. For each n, a and x belong to EuclideanSpace R (Fin n), identified with real n-dimensional Euclidean space with its standard l2 inner product and norm. The function has real values and uses ordinary real division.
quantifiers: For every n in N: if 2 <= n, then for every a in R^n: if ||a|| = 1, then HarmonicOnNhd f_a ({a}^c). Expanded: for every x in R^n with x != a, f_a is C^2 at x and there exists a neighborhood U of x such that for every y in U, the Euclidean Laplacian of f_a at y is zero.
assumptions: The only hypotheses are n >= 2 and ||a|| = 1. In the expanded pointwise conclusion, x != a specifies membership in the conclusion set.
conclusion: The function f_a is HarmonicOnNhd on R^n minus {a}: at each point of that set it is C^2, and its actual Euclidean Laplacian vanishes identically on some neighborhood of that point.
scopes: The conclusion applies to every x != a in the whole Euclidean space; there is no restriction to the unit ball or its boundary. The norm and Laplacian are Euclidean. Harmonicity has exactly the local C^2 and neighborhood-Laplacian sense in the approved definition context. The quotient has its ordinary real-division interpretation; the excluded point a carries no conclusion.
constant_dependencies: The constants 1 in the numerator and unit-norm assumption and 2 in the dimension bound and squared norm are fixed. The denominator exponent is the same dimension n. The function depends on n and a. A neighborhood witnessing harmonicity may depend on n, a, and the point x. There are no additional unspecified constants or uniformity assertions.
